pre_text:
It'll be Bhuvneshwar Kumar to take the new ball. Can he light this contest up like Shaheen Afridi did in Dubai last year? Two slips in place. Here we go!

Rohit leads India's huddle on the outfield. Babar and Rizwan wait pitch-side. Pakistan have been a brilliant chasing team over the last two years but can they post a defendable total after being inserted?

6.55pm: The MCG is rammed. Flags waving in every stand, not a spare seat in the house. The players walk out through the tunnel, and line up for the anthems. Rohit Sharma looks almost overwhelmed by the noise as India's draws to an end. 

Zak: "To break up the millions of Indian/Pakistani comments, as an Aussie, I just got goosebumps with the anthems just now. What a moment that was. Feels like the final all ready!"

Shahzad: "Will have to follow the game while "working" in the office. Alt Tab to the rescue." -- You won't be alone in that.

6.45pm: Thanks, KK. The build-up is nearly over, and the biggest game in cricket at the biggest stadium in Australia is only 15 minutes away. Let me know your thoughts on the teams: surprised that Yuzvendra Chahal has been left out?

Rajesh: "I would have thought this would be the ideal match for Pant. Disrupt the Shadab, Nawaz combination against a completely right hand top order"

Sabith: "This is not the biggest game. The biggest game will be India vs Pakistan final at the very same venue next month :p"

Datta: "Rohit Sharma found a Pep Guardiola. A very left field selection. Will haunt then back"

Adarsh: "Interesting that Shami couldn't find a place in the original squad, and was brought in as a replacement for Bumrah. And he finds a place in the starting XI ahead of Harshal Patel. This points to some inconsistencies in the selection process."

Alex Malcolm at the MCG: "It's very rare to have a T20 game at the MCG this early in the Australian summer. Normally there is only first-class cricket played here at this time of year. Last year this pitch had a lot of spice in it in November and December in red ball cricket, particularly when curator Matt Page left plenty of grass on it. Traditionally white ball pitches at the MCG don't have much grass for the BBL in January. This has a decent covering. It will be intriguing to see if there is swing, seam and bounce for India first up."

Gaurav Sundararaman points out that chasing has been the way to go in India-Pakistan T20Is. The team batting first has not won one since 2012; the chasing team has won the last six.

6.35pm Here are the teams.

Pakistan: 1 Mohammad Rizwan, 2 Babar Azam, 3 Shan Masood, 4 Shadab Khan, 5 Haider Ali, 6 Iftikhar Ahmed, 7 Mohammad Nawaz, 8 Asif Ali, 9 Shaheen Shah Afridi, 10 Naseem Shah, 11 Haris Rauf.

India 1 Rohit Sharma, 2 KL Rahul, 3 Virat Kohli, 4 Suryakumar Yadav, 5 Hardik Pandya, 6 Dinesh Karthik, 7 Axar Patel, 8 R Ashwin, 9 Mohammed Shami, 10 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 11 Arshdeep Singh.

Interesting selection from India. Shami and Ashwin in, Harshal and Chahal out. The rest is along expected lines. Ashwin's selection suggests two things - India are aware of the possibility of Nawaz floating up the order, and are aiming to disrupt this. And they also know that Babar and Rizwan don't really attack offspin that much. And also, Ashwin isn't just an offspinner. Against right-handers, his stock balls come out of the front of the hand - the carrom ball and the reverse carrom ball, and his record against RHBs is top-notch.

Pakistan had a difficult choice to make, to pick three seamers out of the five superb ones they have. They've gone with Shaheeh Shah Afridi, Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah.

With those observations, I'll take a little break, and welcome Matt Roller into the commentary pod.

6.30pm Rohit tosses, Babar calls tails, and it's heads. India will bowl first. 

"Looks like a good pitch, a bit of grass, and it's a little overcast, so the ball might swing around a little bit, so we'll try and use that to our advantage," Rohit says. "Very much sorted with our preparation now. It's time to come out and enjoy ourselves."

Team composition: "Seven batters, an allrounder, three seamers, two spinners." Rohit doesn't say who will fill those roles. And it adds up to 12.

Babar smartly takes the cue from Rohit. "Three fast bowlers, two spinners, and the rest are batsmen." 

6.25pm Around 20 minutes ago (it's gotten a little cloudier since):



6.20pm What does the pitch look like? According to Michael Clarke, it's an "absolute beauty". A bit of green grass on top, and it's "rock hard". "A beautiful batting pitch once you get in, get past that new ball." He suggests that the captain winning the toss bat first. Interesting.

Jiten Chandaran: "It looks like Ashwin is playing, so that means they have some batting at 8, which allows Shami to come in for Harshal. I expect now."

Fiaz Laghari: "A while ago, we friends left our room to get some breakfast and everyone out here on the roads seems to be in a great rush. It's like a storm is coming and people are rushing to some safe place, that is how the excitement level is here in Lahore for Pak-Ind clash. Everyone trying to get their things done before the match starts."

6.15pm Virat Kohli's just given India's players an animated pep talk. We're also hearing that Mohammed Shami is marking out his run-up. If he plays, it'll be his 18th T20I. Half of them, Sampath Bandarupalli informs me, have come at World Cups. That's quite a stat.

Adarsh: "Here's a left-field opinion: India should have Pant open today to create a left-right combination against Shaheen Shah Afridi and hopefully mess with his lines."

BW: "Could this be the most viewed cricinfo commentary of all time? No pressure, Karthik."

6.05pm Monga is watching India train, and his observations tell him Rishabh Pant probably isn't playing tonight. 

"Pakistan have put up three national flags on their warm-up side of the field," Monga adds. "India zero." Make of this what you will.

Syed: "Dreadful weather here in my town Swindon but terrific news about the weather in Melbourne hopefully to watch a full match without interference." -- I don't think this has any basis in science, but the more rain there is in every non-Melbourne city in the world, the less the chances of rain in Melbourne. Swindon is doing its bit for cricket!

Syed Habeeb: "What is the news about Fakhar Zaman?" -- He hasn't recovered fully from his knee issue, so he's not available today.

5.55pm Here are two fantastic pieces on two fantastic Pakistan players: Alex Malcolm chats with the former Melbourne Stars list manager Trent Woodhill about Haris Rauf, who'll come into tonight's game with plenty of local knowledge of the conditions. And Danyal Rasool interviews the ebullient and thoughtful Shadab Khan, Pakistan's Mr. T20.

If you're in the US, you can watch the game live on ESPN+.

If any of you collect player cards, autographed bats or other memorabilia from cricket games, you may be interested in their digital versions. For the fantasy players and gamers among you, you may want to check out a game from our digital collectibles partners Fan Craze - the FanCraze Flash Nets game, where you use digital collectibles to play and earn rewards.

Saurabh: "I have three work colleagues from Pakistan here in Perth. We share and align almost on everything from food to thoughts, from wishing each other on Diwali and Eid. This is the day when we won't align as it is India vs Pak :P"

Kushal mehta: "Have slept for an hour at night, driven 500 km non stop, but never felt more energetic than today. Got my adrenaline rushing high. New Indian t20 jersey on, game on! Go India. Seek Revenge for the previous defeat!"

Sujith: "Early prediction Rauf gets Rohit, Shaheen gets Virat, Bhuvi gets Rizwan, Arshdeep gets Babar."

5.40pm In case you haven't noticed already, our Live Blog is up and running. And if it's expert opinions you're after, who better than Anil Kumble and Stephen Fleming to set things up?

Arun Heer: "Welcome to a clash which is not less than a festival in these two nations playing each other! We're more than 100 members of 'Langley Lions', a cricket team of local players in British Columbia, CANADA, all awake to to watch at 1 AM local time. God will change plans and postpone rain as he has to watch this clash too, agreed??"

Mustafa Moudi : "Last 4 results between these 2 sides in T20I (Oldest first) - India Won (T20 WC '16), Pakistan Won (T20 WC '21), India Won (Asia Cup '22 Group Stage) and Pakistan Won (Asia Cup '22 Super 4). Going by the pattern.... IYKWIM !!"

5.30pm Hello, hello. Welcome to ESPNcricinfo's coverage of the latest chapter in the friendliest, most bonhomious (it's officially a word now) rivalry in all cricket. You'll be pleased to know that Melbourne is bathed in bright sunlight at the moment, judging by the images our correspondent Sidharth Monga is sending over. Fans in blue and green are streaming into the 'G as we speak, having squeezed out of the traffic jam encircling the stadium. We're an hour away from the toss, and we really cannot wait.

Siddharth: "It's time for the greatest sporting event of the year. Can't wait!!"

Hamza: "Hello everyone from Pakistan! Was waiting impatiently for this telecast to get started. Usual stuff, sleepless night. Surely, a contest bewteen quality bowling and batting today. I think India have an edge, they have got quality batting with depth and consistency. Pakistani batters are not reliabale apart from openers. On such difficult batting tracks you need good technic like Indian batsmen. Good luck to both teams."

short_text: Shadab Khan to Pandya, FOUR
commentary: a rare bit of flight, Shadab overpitches this on leg stump, and Hardik brings all his bottom hand into a powerful drive back past the stumps. Long-on had no chance

short_text: Shadab Khan to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: back of a length outside off, punched to sweeper cover

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: back of a length outside off, rocks back and carves it to sweeper cover

short_text: Shadab Khan to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: short and wide, but there's a sweeper out on the boundary, and Hardik's cut gets only one run

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, 2 runs
commentary: steps out, meets this off-stump ball on the full, and whips it firmly to the left of deep midwicket

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Pandya, SIX
commentary: makes himself a lot of room in advance, and Nawaz tries to follow him with a flat slider. Doesn't cramp him enough, and Hardik clears his front leg and swipes it away over the midwicket boundary. Made a difficult hit look easy
pre_text: Nawaz to bowl his third.

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: flat, back of a length, finishing just outside off. Flat-batted firmly to long-on

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, no run
commentary: appeal for a bat-pad catch as the ball balloons to Rizwan moving into the backward short leg area. Flat, speared into the pads, and Kohli missed the flick. Given not out, and Pakistan have reviewed! Nope, absolutely no bat on this. Straight off pad, and the pad was well outside leg stump at the point of impact, so there's no chance of lbw either. Ultra edge is looked at anyway, for academic purposes

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, SIX
commentary: shot! Jumps out of his crease, stepping leg-side to create swinging room, and he gets into the perfect position against this middle-and-leg ball to launch it high and straight, back over the non-striker's head

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: flat length ball straightening towards off stump, nurdled into the midwicket region

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Pandya, SIX
commentary: wow, that's proper power. Flat, speared in on off stump, and Hardik clears his front leg and mows it over long-on, clearing the fielder comfortably even though he was interested for 2/3rds of the ball's flight

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: steps out, and Afridi sees him coming. Spears it wide of off stump. Reaches out to try anb stab it away, edges it down to deep third
pre_text: Twenty off that over, and it prompts a bowling change. Afridi returns. Round the wicket to Kohli.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pandya, 2 runs
commentary: length ball, looks like the slower ball angling into leg stump, hangs back and tucks it gently into the square leg region. That ensures they get two, with all the leg-side fielders in front of square back on the boundary

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: low full-toss outside off, and Hardik may feel he's missed out. Flat-bats it, doesn't quite middle it, and cover dives left to stop the ball

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: nicely done. Back of a length, angling into the legs, and Kohli tucks it away neatly, timing it superbly and beating deep fine leg to his right

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: down the track now and Shaheen fires a full one into the stumps. Plays a checked flick that hangs briefly in the air before rolling out to deep midwicket

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pandya, no run
commentary: brilliant. Fast yorker, angling into middle stump from round the wicket, and Hardik plays it respectfully, pulling his front leg out of the way and jamming his bat down to squeeze it into the pitch
pre_text: Mid-off drops back, third man comes into the circle.

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: short and wide, and that's a poor ball with cover point in the circle and extra-cover back on the boundary. Beats cover point to his right with the cut, and the deep fielder was left with far too much to do
pre_text: Shadab changes ends.

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: tossed up slow and wide of off stump. Stretches out and flat-bats a drive to long-off

short_text: Shadab Khan to Pandya, no run
commentary: misses out. Short and wide, and he fails to beat backward point with his cut

short_text: Shadab Khan to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: shortish on the stumps, worked away to deep midwicket

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, no run
commentary: steps out and Shadab slows it down and shortens his length on leg stump. Looks to flick, misses, and the ball rolls off the pad into the point region

short_text: Shadab Khan to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: looped up wide of off stump, gets down on back knee to sweep along the floor to deep midwicket

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, 2 runs
commentary: trademark Kohli. Slower offcutter on off stump, and he clips it gently into the midwicket region, aware that all the fielders in front of square there are on the boundary. Immediately calls for two, legs pumping
pre_text: Right. So Pakistan have one over of spin left. I suspect they'll hold it back as long as possible - as was the case in the first Asia Cup meeting between these sides a couple of months ago. India need 70 off 36. Here's Naseem.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: well bowled. Slower bouncer, gets it up to shoulder height outside off. Rolls the wrists over the pull to deep midwicket

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: back of the hand slower ball, turns in like a googly and finishes at chest height. Pulled to deep midwicket

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: shot! Steps out, and Naseem tries to cramp him with the full ball at his feet. Ends up a little too leg-side, though, and Kohli flicks it away and beats the diving short fine leg fielder to his left

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: steps out again, gets a little too close to the pitch of this stump-to-stump ball to be able to attack it. Clips it down to long-on

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: another short wrong'un, finishes around chest height and Hardik pulls to deep square leg
pre_text: Aby : "Pakistan after 14 overs were 98/5 . Just 8 runs ahead . If India hold their nerve . They might just scrap across the line "

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, no run
commentary: short outside off, extra bounce beats Hardik's attempted cut
pre_text: Right then. 60 off 30. You'd back India if they had seven or eight wickets in hand. They only have five, with not much batting to come after Dinesh Karthik. Here's Haris Rauf.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: back of a length on off stump, makes room and steers it down to deep third

short_text: Haris Rauf to Kohli, no run
commentary: quick, hard length, angling into leg stump. Looks to flick, ends up playing it back to the bowler off the high part of the bat. 148kph
pre_text: Akram: "India have given unnecessary respect to Shaheen today. He has bowled nowhere close to what his figures suggest today. That's the impact he has left in the minds of Indian batters one year after that match!"

short_text: Haris Rauf to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: back of a length outside off, flat-batted to the left of mid-off. May have snatched at it a little there. The square cut may have been on

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 3 wides
commentary: short, angling down leg, Hardik aborts his attempt to pull, and Rizwan, flying to his left, gets the edge of his glove to the ball to prevent it from running down to the boundary

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, no run
commentary: slower legcutter outside off, and Hardik misses the attempted flat-bat off drive

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: back of a length close to off stump, tucked away into the midwicket region, but no second run this time, with Shadab hurtling in off the deep midwicket boundary to cut it off

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: full, angling into the legs. Knew Hardik was looking to clear his front leg there, and cramped him for room. Shovelled on the bounce to deep midwicket
pre_text: 54 from 24. Naseem to bowl. Monga tells us Pakistan have 23 minutes to bowl the last 4 overs. Which means they're unlikely to run into the over-rate penalty.

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, 2 runs
commentary: makes room, and Naseem bowls a slower short ball on off stump. Flat-bats it, but can't find much power. Clears extra-cover but the ball plops down on the outfield

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, no run
commentary: again looks to make room, and again Naseem bowls the slower short ball, just outside off. Throws his bat at it, looking to carve it away, but can't connect

short_text: Naseem Shah to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: full, near-yorker at the stumps, clipped to deep midwicket. The longer boundary is to the leg side this over

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, no run
commentary: another slower short ball, outside off. Looks to pull, and ends up bottom-edging it on the bounce to the right of Rizwan, who dives and prevents the single

short_text: Naseem Shah to Pandya, 2 runs
commentary: short outside off, gets it to kick up quite high. Manages to keep the pull down to the right of deep midwicket, and they hurry through for two. Superb over, just the six runs off it

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: stunning. Shot of Kohli's innings so far, and it brings up his fifty. Looks for the hard length, errs slightly on the short side, and Kohli pulls it firmly and finds the gap to the right of deep midwicket. Nearly clears the boundary too, but it's one-bounce
pre_text: 48 off the last three. Nawaz still has that one over remaining, but India can't bank entirely on that one over. Shaheen comes back to bowl his fourth. Third man and fine leg inside the circle. Round the wicket.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, 1 wide
commentary: looks to spear in the yorker, ends up slanting it down the leg side. Left alone

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, 2 runs
commentary: looks for the yorker again, bowls a low full-toss angling into middle and leg. Makes room and drives to deep cover

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: Lovely placement, and he's managed to get just enough power on it. Makes room, and Afridi looks to follow him with the yorker. Can't quite get his line or length right, and Kohli lifts the low full-toss over extra-cover, and manages to dribble the ball over the boundary, beating long-off and sweeper cover in the process

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: short, shoulder-high on the stumps. The pull hits the high part of the bat and rolls down to the right of long-on
pre_text: Over the wicket now.

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: shortish slower ball finishing wide of off stump, flat-batted to extra-cover

short_text: Shaheen Shah Afridi to Kohli, FOUR
commentary: shot, and it's gone all the way! Terrific, swivelling hook from Kohli! Shaheen goes short, and it ends up just above hip high. steps across, swivels on his back leg, and helps the ball over short fine leg. Times it absolutely perfectly too

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: Length ball angling into the corridor, sits deep in his crease and flat-bats it along the ground to deep midwicket
pre_text: Well then. It's down to 31 off 12. What a partnership this has been. Rauf to finish off, which means Nawaz will bowl the 20th.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Kohli, 1 run
commentary: length ball outside off, slapped on the bounce to deep cover point

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, no run
commentary: extra bounce. Short outside off, and the ball beats Hardik's attempted uppercut
pre_text: That's the 100 partnership, by the way.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Pandya, 1 run
commentary: hard length., angling into the body. Can't pull that, just manages to send it dribbling towards long-on off the sticker of the bat
pre_text: What a performance so far from Haris. Three more balls to deliver.

short_text: Haris Rauf to Kohli, SIX
commentary: okay, wow. Has Kohli ever played a better shot in T20 cricket? Length ball, finishing around bail-high, and Kohli punches it with an almost straight bat, straight back over the bowler's head. Swivels through the hip a little as he does so, a la Jos Buttler, and it easily carries over the rope

short_text: Haris Rauf to Kohli, SIX
commentary: fullish, angling into leg stump, and Kohli has caused the MCG to explode into pure noise. A flick of the wrists, and the ball sails over the boundary to the left of fine leg. Wow!

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Pandya, OUT
commentary: got him, what a strike for Pakistan! Flat, speared into the pads, and Hardik loses his shape completely as he tries to slog this over the leg side. Edges it, and the ball balloons to the fielder at cover point
pre_text:
Mohammad Rizwan is standing back to the spinner! Deep extra-cover, long-off, long-on, cow corner, deep square leg are back.
 
Fifteen off that over. Twelve off those last two balls. And it comes down to 16 off this final over, with Mohammad Nawaz to bowl. What an incredible game this has been. What an innings Virat Kohli has played.
dismissal: HH Pandya c Babar Azam b Mohammad Nawaz 40 (61m 37b 1x4 2x6) SR: 108.1

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Karthik, 1 run
commentary: down the track, and he gets a full-toss that's chest-high when he meets it. Would it have been as high if he was standing in his normal position? Probably not. Swatted down to long-on
pre_text: And with the new T20I rules in place, it'll be Dinesh Karthik on strike and not Kohli, even though the batters crossed over. DK isn't the greatest of starters against spin, usually...

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, 2 runs
commentary: they need a boundary every ball, almost, but they only get two here. Very full, almost a wide yorker, and Kohli drags it down to long-on, all along the ground
pre_text: Kohli on strike. Fifteen to win off four balls. Fourteen to tie. Nawaz is basically bowling left-arm medium.

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, (no ball) SIX
commentary: full-toss, full-toss, and it's gone for six!!!! It's only just gone for six, but it's gone for six nonetheless! On off stump, and it's a fairly high full-toss too - it's been called no-ball!!! - and Kohli swats it away over the leg side. Deep square leg leaps to his right, gets a hand to the ball to try and flap it back into play, but it still lands beyond the rope

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, 1 wide
commentary: now he bowls a wide! All the pressure is on the poor bowler, and he looks to keep it away from Kohli's reach, but ends up spearing his wide yorker beyond the off-side tramline
pre_text: Suddenly, India need 6 off 3. Such a massive difference from 13 off 3.

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Kohli, 3 byes
commentary: bowled him, but it's a free hit! And they run three by the time the throw comes in from the third man region!!! Full, angling into off stump, and Kohli misses his attempted sweep. But he knows it's a free-hit, and he sets off at full pace, as does DK. The ball rolls between the keeper and short third, and they pick up three byes
pre_text: Five off three.

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Karthik, OUT
commentary: got him, a stumping off the pads!!! Goes flat, angling down leg, following DK's movement to make room. Looks to sweep, and the ball dribbles off the pad behind the wicket. And Rizwan is alert to the fact that DK has stumbled out of his crease. What a moment. Rizwan is well down the leg side when he collects the ball, and he falls to his right to complete the stumping
pre_text: Phew. It's down to two off two now, with DK on strike. Absolutely incredible scenes at the G. Do Pakistan bring their fielders in to crowd the ring? Nope, just four inside the circle. Keeper comes back up to the stumps.
dismissal: KD Karthik st †Mohammad Rizwan b Mohammad Nawaz 1 (10m 2b 0x4 0x6) SR: 50

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Ashwin, 1 wide
commentary: and Nawaz bowls a wide!!!! Expects Ashwin to try and make room, maybe, and sends a flat, quick one well down the leg side. Ashwin just watches it pass him, and the MCG explodes once more!
pre_text: Whodathunkit. R Ashwin to face the last ball, with two runs needed. One to tie. Still just four inside the circle.

short_text: Mohammad Nawaz to Ashwin, 1 run
commentary: and Ashwin clears one of those infielders!!! What a cool, collected, and elegant finish!!! Full, angling into the stumps, and Ashwin makes a little bit of room and scoops the ball over mid-off. What a finish! What a freaking game!!!
pre_text: Seven fielders in the circle now.
